title: Integral ring-object constructibility and the completed category
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, and a finite intermediate field $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, with valuation ring $A=\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $Z$ be a Noetherian finite-dimensional scheme on which $\ell$ is invertible: $Z$ is quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme] and locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth], so it has a finite affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings, a finite bound on chains of irreducible closed subsets [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], and $\ell$ is a unit in every local ring. Put $B_Z=p_Z^*\underline A$ [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring, sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Identify it with $\varprojlim_{n\ge1}(A/\varpi^n)_Z$ by the canonical coefficient-limit map [sk-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x]. In the ordinary category $D(\operatorname{Mod}(B_Z))$ [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories], for every $K$ the following conditions are equivalent:

(i) $K$ is bounded constructible in the general ring-object sense [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible]: its cohomology vanishes outside a finite interval and, after a finite constructible locally closed stratification, each cohomology sheaf is pro-étale locally a cokernel of a finite matrix over $B_Z$.

(ii) $K$ belongs to the derived-complete integral category [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]: it is derived $\varpi$-complete, and its derived reductions $K_n=K\otimes^L_{B_Z}(A/\varpi^n)_Z$ have compatible étale-origin representatives with classical constructible cohomology, all in a single cohomological interval independent of $n$.

(iii) $K$ is bounded and its cohomology sheaves, after finite stratification, are pro-étale locally $B_V\otimes_A P$ for finitely presented scalar $A$-modules $P$ [sk-def-sfb-constructible]; here $A$ and $P$ in this tensor denote constant sheaves. The stratifications in (i) and (iii) may differ. Torsion cohomology is allowed, and no completeness hypothesis is imposed in (i).
